title: Chain of interlocking oval links
purpose: Build a chain of oval (stadium) wire links that hook through each other, as one link mesh instanced by glTF nodes at alternating 90 degree angles. Use it for props, rigging and anchors.

entry_points.name: stadium_point
entry_points.summary: (position, unit tangent) on the stadium centre line in the XZ plane at arc-length ``fraction`` in [0, 1), starting at the middle of the +Z straight side and running counter-clockwise seen from +Y.

entry_points.name: link_mesh
entry_points.summary: One closed link in the XZ plane centred at the origin: samples * sides vertices and quads (torus topology). The centre line is planar, so the frame is the in-plane normal and +Y.

entry_points.name: chain
entry_points.signature: chain(links=7, straight=0.4, end_radius=0.3, wire_radius=0.08, clearance=0.02, samples=64, sides=12)
entry_points.summary: A scene dict {"meshes": [link], "nodes": [...]}: a root node and one child node per link along X.

entry_points.name: chain_mesh
entry_points.signature: chain_mesh(links=7, straight=0.4, end_radius=0.3, wire_radius=0.08, clearance=0.02, samples=64, sides=12)
entry_points.summary: The chain baked into one mesh (each link transformed by its node), for measuring and for OBJ.

entry_points.name: main
entry_points.summary: Command line: write the chain (instanced nodes in .gltf, baked in .obj) and print a JSON summary.

parameters.name: straight
parameters.meaning: Length of the straight sides of each link's centre line.

parameters.name: end_radius
parameters.meaning: Radius of the round ends of the centre line; above 2 * wire_radius + clearance.

parameters.name: clearance
parameters.meaning: Gap left between neighbouring links where they hook.

parameters.name: samples
parameters.meaning: Samples along each link's centre line.

contract.complexity: O(samples * sides) for the link; O(links) nodes

outputs.content: one link mesh and a root node with one child node per link (instancing)
the chain with every link transformed into place

limits: Links are rigid and straight in a line; there is no physics or sag. Contact is only avoided geometrically when end_radius exceeds twice the wire radius plus the clearance (checked). No texture coordinates.
technique_references: Stadium centre line with arc-length parameter
glTF node instancing with quaternion rotations
